title: Label-Guided Representation Learning for Incomplete Multi-View Multi-Label Classification
claim: A multi-stage framework turns label semantics into priors that guide representation learning and then drive probabilistic fusion for prediction.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, color-coded tinted containers, with cross-panel arrows
description: A wide three-panel overview with a differently tinted rounded container for each panel. Panel (a), blue, shows embeddings passing through an encoder to colored category prototypes. These feed a sphere diagram where the prototypes act as direction vectors, and a Gaussian mixture panel where observed labels make positive samples attract and negative samples repel. Panel (b), gray, shows incomplete multi-view inputs with missing cells going through an encoder, latent features z, a decoder and a classifier. Feature consistency and label consistency are shown as overlapping distributions, linked to the latent and output spaces. Panel (c), pink, shows the category prior, sampling, product-of-posteriors fusion, full and single view branches with classifiers, and confidence weighting, ending in the final prediction ŷ. Orange, green and blue stacked slabs and small bar charts carry the data flow.
caption: Overview of LGRL. (a) Semantic-Informed Mixture Prior encodes label relationships via learnable category prototypes. (b) Task-Relevant Representation Learning enforces consistency at both feature and label levels. (c) Bayesian Fusion integrates category priors into posterior computation for hypothesis-based prediction.
abstract: Incomplete multi-view multi-label classification addresses scenarios where views and labels are partially missing. While existing methods treat labels solely as supervision signals, they overlook the semantic structure inherent in partial annotations. We propose Label-Guided Representation Learning (LGRL) that systematically exploits label semantics as structural priors throughout learning. Our framework constructs a semantic-informed mixture prior via learnable category prototypes to guide representation extraction, and introduces category-specific conditional posteriors where prototypes act as Bayesian experts for multi-view fusion. We further derive a principled label-driven information bottleneck objective balancing reconstruction sufficiency with cross-view consistency, enabling category-conditional reasoning. Extensive experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of LGRL across benchmark datasets as well as real-world applications in sports analytics and medical imaging.
